extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners interested in peer review analysis and datasets
extracted.subtask_description: Release and analysis of PeerRead, a dataset of scientific peer reviews (paper drafts, accept/reject decisions, and textual reviews) and demonstration of two NLP tasks: predicting acceptance and predicting numerical review-aspect scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition: 14.7K paper drafts and accept/reject decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset consists of 14.7K paper drafts and the corresponding accept/reject decisions in top-tier venues including ACL, NIPS and ICLR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the labeled corpus (papers + binary decisions) that enables study and modeling of acceptance outcomes; emphasizes coverage of top-tier venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual peer reviews: 10.7K reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset also includes 10.7K textual peer reviews written by experts for a subset of the papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These expert-written review texts are available for analysis and for training models that operate on review language (e.g., predicting scores or extracting critique).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predict paper acceptance (binary classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Task: predict whether a paper is accepted. The paper reports that simple models can predict whether a paper is accepted with up to 21% error reduction compared to the majority baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation uses error reduction relative to a majority-class baseline as a key metric; simple baseline models produce measurable improvement (up to 21% error reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predict numerical scores of review aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Task: predict the numerical scores of review aspects (per-review aspect ratings). The authors show simple models can outperform the mean baseline for aspects with high variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparison baseline is the mean prediction; aspects exhibiting higher variance (across reviews) are where models can most improve upon the mean baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review aspects (examples: 'originality' and 'impact')
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of review aspects included in the dataset are 'originality' and 'impact', which are cited as aspects with high variance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These aspect labels serve as explicit prediction targets in the dataset; the paper highlights them as illustrative aspects where modeling shows gains.
